    "title": "Equipment Allocation for Profit Maximization",
    "source": "Lab 1",
    "statement": "A plant produces three types of products on four types of equipment with specified processing times, available working hours, and unit profits. Formulate a linear program to determine the production quantity of each product type that maximizes total profit."
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Bounded Feasible Space Objective Optimization",
    "source": "Lab 1",
    "statement": "Maximize and minimize the objective function F(x1, x2) = x1 + x2 subject to 2x1 + 4x2 <= 16, -4x1 + 2x2 <= 8, x1 + 3x2 >= 9, and nonnegativity constraints using the graphical method."
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Alternative Optimal Solutions Along Boundary Segment",
    "source": "Lab 1",
    "statement": "Maximize and minimize F(x1, x2) = x1 + 2x2 subject to 2x1 + 4x2 <= 16, -4x1 + 2x2 <= 8, x1 + 3x2 >= 9, and nonnegativity constraints using the graphical method."
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Inconsistent Constraint System Evaluation",
    "source": "Lab 1",
    "statement": "Maximize and minimize x1 + x2 subject to x1 + 2x2 >= 14, -5x1 + 3x2 <= 15, 4x1 + 6x2 <= 24, and nonnegativity constraints using the graphical method."
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Iterative Slack Dictionary Optimization",
    "source": "Lab 1",
    "statement": "Solve the linear program maximizing F(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6) = 2x1 + 3x2 - x4 subject to three linear equality constraints and nonnegativity conditions using the simplex method."
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Paint Production Graphical Profit Maximization",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Determine the daily amounts of exterior and interior paints to maximize total profit z = 5x1 + 4x2 subject to raw material availabilities, market demand limits, and nonnegativity constraints using the graphical method."
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Feed Mix Graphical Cost Minimization",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Determine the daily minimum-cost feed mix of corn and soybean meal minimizing z = 0.3x1 + 0.9x2 subject to total weight, protein percentage, fiber percentage, and nonnegativity constraints using the graphical method."
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Paint Production Profit Maximization Formulation",
    "source": "Lecture 2",
    "statement": "Formulate a two-variable linear programming model for Tatar-Paint to maximize daily profit from exterior and interior paints subject to raw material availability and market demand limits."
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Feed Mix Minimum Cost Formulation",
    "source": "Lecture 2",
    "statement": "Formulate a linear programming model for Ozark Farms to determine the daily minimum-cost mix of corn and soybean meal satisfying total weight, minimum protein, and maximum fiber requirements."
  }
